Definition: a primary verb; to look at (literally or figuratively):--behold, beware, lie, look (on, to), perceive, regard, see, sight, take heed. Compare G3700.
BiblicalUsage: To see is the word for looking, perceiving, taking heed — and it appears over a hundred times. In Matthew 5:28 Jesus says whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart. In Matthew 7:3 he asks why we behold the mote in our brother's eye. In John 1:29 John says, behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world. And in Hebrews 11:1 faith is the evidence of things not seen.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two lookings are the whole Christian life: the look that lusts, and the look that beholds the Lamb — and faith is the sight of what cannot be seen.
